scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8875: Users in both pods report the "web1.local" portal
stopped loading. DNS still resolves web1.local to 10.200.0.4, and the other
portals (web0/web2/web3) all load fine. From user machines, ping 10.200.0.4
gets no reply -- yet the server team says web_server_1 is up, Apache is
running, and the dns_server can still ping 10.200.0.4 from inside the farm.
Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: web_server_1 default-route (gateway) configuration
Mechanism: web_server_1 (10.200.0.4) normally reaches off-subnet clients via
  its default route through the farm gateway 10.200.0.1 on
  switch_server_access. With the default route deleted, the server can only
  talk to 10.200.0.0/24. Requests from the user pods still ARRIVE (the OSPF
  path and DNS are healthy), but every reply to a 10.1.1.x / 10.2.1.x source
  is unroutable on the server and is dropped -- so pings time out and HTTP
  never completes, while intra-farm reachability (dns_server -> 10.200.0.4)
  keeps working. Scope is exactly one server; web0/web2/web3 are untouched.
Localization: web_server_1
Root cause: default route (via 10.200.0.1) missing on web_server_1
Fix: `ip route add default via 10.200.0.1 dev eth0` on web_server_1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip route add default via 10.200.0.1 dev eth0` on web_server_1
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing default (gateway) route on the server

bonus-exonerates-network: notes DNS resolution, the OSPF path, and the other web servers are healthy, so nothing network-side needs fixing

agent.diagnosis_text:
web_server_1 (10.200.0.4/24) is missing its default gateway. Every other
host in the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm — web_server_0, web_server_2,
web_server_3, and dns_server — carries the entry "default via 10.200.0.1
dev eth0", pointing at the switch_server_access bridge interface (br0,
10.200.0.1/24). web_server_1 has only its directly-connected route
(10.200.0.0/24) and nothing else.

The mechanism that produces the exact observed asymmetry is classic black-
hole return-path failure. Inbound traffic reaches web_server_1 correctly:
the OSPF domain advertises 10.200.0.0/24 via switch_server_access, so
router_core_3 forwards user packets into the server segment. web_server_1
receives those packets but, when it tries to send the reply to a user
address (e.g. 10.1.1.x or 10.2.1.x), the kernel finds no route and
silently drops the datagram. From the user side this looks like a silent
timeout — exactly what helpdesk reports. dns_server (10.200.0.2) lives in
the same /24, so its ping replies use the directly-connected route and
succeed, corroborating the "server is up" claim from the server team.
Apache is genuinely running; the fault is purely at the IP routing layer of
the host OS.

Root cause: web_server_1's startup configuration omits the default gateway,
leaving it with no route to any destination outside 10.200.0.0/24.

Corrective fix: Add a persistent default route on web_server_1:
  ip route add default via 10.200.0.1 dev eth0
and record it in the lab's startup script so it survives reboots. No
router, switch, or daemon changes are required.
